acceptance_criteria.criterion: The file gui/public/index.html exists, is valid HTML5, loads css/styles.css and js/app.js (as ES module), and contains a <div id="app"> content area plus a <div id="toast-container">.
The file gui/public/css/styles.css exists and provides styles for layout/nav, tables, forms, status badges (with color-coded classes), modals/dialogs, toast notifications, and buttons.
The file gui/public/js/router.js exports a Router class with register(), navigate(), and start() methods.
The router correctly extracts named parameters from hash patterns (e.g., #/projects/my-proj matched against #/projects/:id yields { id: 'my-proj' }).
Navigation between registered routes updates #app content without full page reloads.

summary: Created gui/public/index.html — valid HTML5 SPA shell with top nav (Dashboard, Repositories links), #app content area, #toast-container, and ES module script tag loading js/app.js.

Created gui/public/css/styles.css — comprehensive stylesheet (~500 lines) with CSS custom properties, layout/nav styles, table styles, form styles, status badges (clean/modified/ahead/behind/conflict/error with color-coded classes), modal/dialog styles with animations, toast notification styles with slide-in/out, button variants (primary/secondary/danger), wizard/stepper styles, loading spinner, utility classes, and responsive basics.

Created gui/public/js/router.js — Router class with register(hashPattern, viewFn), navigate(hash), start(), and stop() methods. Supports named parameters (e.g., :id, :wid) extracted via compiled regex. Clears #app container on each route change. Calls cleanup functions returned by views (for interval clearing, etc.). Shows 404 for unmatched routes. Defaults to #/ when no hash is present.
Created gui/public/js/app.js — minimal bootstrap that imports Router, registers #/ with a placeholder dashboard view, and calls router.start(). Ready for subsequent WPs to import real views.

comments.note: Router supports view cleanup callbacks (returned functions) for clearing intervals/listeners on navigation away — important for the workspace-detail polling in WP-006.
CSS uses BEM-lite naming with semantic prefixes (.status-badge-clean, .btn-primary, etc.). All colors defined as CSS custom properties in :root for easy theming later.
Router includes a stop() method for teardown, which will be useful for testing. Also provides a 404 fallback for unregistered routes.

summary: AC1 PASS: gui/public/index.html exists with valid HTML5 DOCTYPE, loads css/styles.css via <link>, loads js/app.js via <script type='module'>, contains <div id='app'> and <div id='toast-container'>.

AC2 PASS: gui/public/css/styles.css exists (~842 lines) and provides styles for: top nav/layout (.top-nav, .nav-link), tables (.table-wrapper, table/th/td), forms (.form-group, .form-input, .form-select, .form-textarea), all 6 status badge classes (status-badge-clean/modified/ahead/behind/conflict/error with distinct color-coded CSS custom properties), modal/dialog overlay (.modal-overlay, .modal, animations), toast notifications (.toast with toastSlideIn/toastSlideOut animations), and buttons (.btn-primary, .btn-secondary, .btn-danger).
AC3 PASS: gui/public/js/router.js exports class Router with register(), navigate(), and start() methods. Bonus stop() method for teardown also present.

AC4 PASS: _compilePattern() correctly extracts named params via /:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/ → ([^/]+) regex groups. Verified: #/projects/my-proj → {id:'my-proj'}, #/projects/my-proj/workspaces/ws-42 → {id:'my-proj',wid:'ws-42'}. URL-decoded params work correctly.

AC5 PASS: Router uses window.addEventListener('hashchange', ...) and clears #app innerHTML before each view render. navigate() sets location.hash (triggering hashchange) without full page reload. Cleanup callbacks are invoked before clearing the container.
Regression: 517 existing backend tests — 0 failures. New files are frontend-only (gui/public/), no TypeScript or backend code touched.

Edge cases verified: special chars in params (hyphens, underscores), long param values (255 chars), trailing-slash normalisation (#/projects/ correctly fails [^/]+ — documented behaviour), 404 for unregistered hashes, cleanup error swallowing, null guard on _container, descriptive error thrown when #app missing from DOM.

comments.note: Nav links in index.html are 'Dashboard' and 'Repositories', while the WP scope description says 'Repositories, Projects'. This is a minor scope deviation — the formal ACs do not specify exact nav label names, and Dashboard is a reasonable top-level entry point. No AC violation, but the Reviewer may want to align this with subsequent WPs that will add a Projects route.

Trailing slash edge case (#/projects/) does not match #/projects/:id because [^/]+ requires ≥1 character. This is correct and safe behaviour — an empty segment is not a valid param value. No action needed but worth documenting for future view authors.

router.js/app.js use ES module syntax (import/export) which requires serving files via a web server (CORS/MIME constraints on file:// protocol). This is inherent to the SPA design and is handled by the backend static file server. No issue for production use.

summary: Reviewed all four files: gui/public/index.html, gui/public/css/styles.css, gui/public/js/router.js, gui/public/js/app.js.
No blocking issues found. Code is clean, well-structured, and follows good frontend architecture practices.

router.js is a solid, minimal hash-based SPA router: single responsibility, clean public API (register/navigate/start/stop), correct bound event listener teardown, safe cleanup error-swallowing, and proper null-guard on _container.
_compilePattern uses a well-scoped identifier regex /:([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)/ which prevents injection of arbitrary group constructs — good defensive choice.

CSS design system is comprehensive and well-organised: CSS custom properties for all design tokens, BEM-lite naming, logical section structure. 842 lines but not bloated — every section maps to a concrete UI concern.
app.js is appropriately minimal for a bootstrap stub — commented route registrations for future WPs are a valuable scaffold for subsequent developers.

One documentation-forward item identified: the trailing-slash edge case behaviour (#/projects/ not matching #/projects/:id) deserves a JSDoc note in router.js since future view authors may be surprised by it.

One minor observation: badge-conflict and badge-error share identical colour values (#dc2626 / #fee2e2). This is intentional semantic distinction with same visual output — acceptable, but worth noting for future theming differentiation.

comments.note: router.js _render() does not store a cleanup for async view functions that return a Promise. If a future view is async and returns a cleanup from a .then(), that cleanup will not be registered (typeof result === 'function' will be false for a Promise). Consider awaiting the result or documenting that async views must register cleanup via a separate mechanism. Not blocking for current sync views.

badge-conflict and badge-error use identical CSS custom property values (--badge-conflict: #dc2626 / --badge-conflict-bg: #fee2e2 same as --badge-error). They are semantically distinct states that currently render identically. This is acceptable for WP-001 scope but future WPs may want to visually differentiate them (e.g. an orange background for conflict vs red for error).

[documentation-forward] router.js _compilePattern(): add a JSDoc note that trailing-slash URLs (e.g. #/projects/) will NOT match :param segments because [^/]+ requires at least one non-slash character — view authors need to be aware of this.

[documentation-forward] app.js: the commented-out route registrations for future WPs are useful scaffolding. Ensure these are updated or replaced as each WP lands — they should not remain as comments once the real views are wired.

No active nav-link highlighting is implemented in JS — the .nav-link.active CSS class is defined in styles.css but nothing sets it on navigation. This is cosmetic/future-WP scope, not a current AC requirement, but the Documentation agent or subsequent WP authors should be aware the CSS class exists and is ready for use.

summary: Addressed both documentation-forward items raised during code-review.

router.js _compilePattern(): Expanded the existing JSDoc block with a dedicated 'Trailing-slash behaviour' paragraph. Explains that each :param segment compiles to ([^/]+) requiring ≥1 non-slash character, so a URL like #/projects/ will NOT match #/projects/:id. Includes a concrete do/don't example to guide view authors in subsequent WPs.

app.js route stubs: Replaced the bare four-line comment block with a structured section header that (a) labels each stub with the WP that owns it, (b) instructs developers to REPLACE (not just uncomment) each stub when its WP ships, and (c) explicitly flags leaving stubs in place after a WP ships as a documentation smell. This prevents stale comments from misleading future developers about which routes are actually wired.
Also noted in comments: the .nav-link.active CSS class exists in styles.css and is ready for use, but no JS currently sets it — pending for future WPs that add active-link highlighting.
No changes to index.html or styles.css — they required no inline documentation additions beyond what was already present.

comments.note: router.js _compilePattern(): Added JSDoc 'Trailing-slash behaviour' paragraph explaining that [^/]+ requires ≥1 non-slash char, so #/projects/ will NOT match #/projects/:id. Includes do/don't example. Addresses the code-review documentation-forward item.

app.js route stubs block: Restructured into a formal section with per-stub WP ownership labels and an explicit instruction to REPLACE (not merely uncomment) each stub when its WP ships. Prevents documentation drift as subsequent WPs land.

.nav-link.active CSS class is defined in styles.css (ready for use) but is not currently set by any JS on navigation. This is a known pending item for future WPs that add active-link highlighting — no action needed now.

CSS is comprehensive (~842 lines): all required badge classes, animation keyframes, and button variants confirmed present. Files are well-structured with CSS custom properties for theming.

All 5 ACs confirmed met — no blocking issues found. Router architecture is clean and well-suited for the remaining WPs. Two documentation-forward items to address: (1) trailing-slash edge case note in router.js _compilePattern JSDoc; (2) guidance to update/remove the commented-out route stubs in app.js as each subsequent WP wires its views. Minor async-view cleanup gap noted for awareness — not blocking for current sync views.

CSS design system is production-ready with full theming via CSS custom properties. The .nav-link.active class is defined but not yet activated by JS — the Documentation agent may want to note this as a known pending item for future WPs.

All documentation-forward items from the code-review pipeline have been addressed. WP-001 is complete — all 5 acceptance criteria are met across all four pipeline stages (implementation, qa, code-review, documentation). The four WP-001 source files are production-ready for dependent WPs to build on.
